subject: golden wheel spider
title: This Spider Cartwheels Up to 44 Times a Second to Escape Wasps

scenes.text: This spider's best escape is to stop running and turn into a wheel.
The golden wheel spider lives in Namib Desert dunes, in a burrow up to half a metre deep.
Its enemy, a spider wasp, paralyzes it and lays an egg on its still-living body.
In a straight fight, the wasp usually wins.
So on a steep dune, the spider flips sideways, tucks its legs and rolls, up to 44 turns a second.
It tumbles away at about a metre a second. No running needed. Just a wheel.

description:
The golden wheel spider escapes its deadliest enemy by turning into a wheel.
This huntsman spider (Carparachne aureoflava), about 2 cm long, lives in silk-lined burrows 40 to 50 cm deep in the dunes of Namibia's Namib Desert. Pompilid spider wasps sting and paralyze it and lay an egg on it, and the larva feeds on the living spider. When threatened on a slope, the spider flips onto its side and cartwheels down the dune at about 1 metre per second; counts of its spin range from about 20 to 44 turns per second.
What's the strangest escape trick you've seen an animal use?
first_comment: The spider's burrow can be half a metre deep, and the wasp still digs it out. Would you rather dig or roll?
